title: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP: protect files sent over FTP and SFTP
summary: The briefing passes: its rollout facts, opt-in default, licensing, storage charges and control paths are supported. Add the Endpoint DLP offline-device documentation to support the explanation of policy enforcement before devices receive updates.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP can monitor and protect sensitive data transferred over FTP and SFTP from managed Windows devices.
claims.quote: Endpoint data loss prevention (DLP) in Microsoft Purview can monitor and protect sensitive data transferred over FTP and SFTP from managed Windows devices.

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP evaluates these transfers against policy rules as it does USB copying and network-share activities.
claims.quote: Endpoint DLP evaluates these transfers against your policy rules, just as it does other device activities such as copying to USB devices or network shares.

claims.claim: FTP and SFTP transfer events appear in Activity explorer.
claims.quote: FTP and SFTP events will appear as a new activity type in Activity Explorer.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: FTP and SFTP protection is admin-opt-in, not enabled by default, and existing rules do not automatically gain enforcement.
claims.quote: FTP and SFTP protection is not enabled by default. Administrators must configure FTP/SFTP transfer activities in Endpoint DLP policies to apply protection.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; changes
claims.claim: An administrator enables FTP and SFTP protection by selecting the FTP and SFTP transfers activity in a device policy rule.
claims.quote:
Under Actions, select Audit or restrict activities on devices.
5. In File activities for all apps, select Apply restrictions to specific activity.
6. Select the FTP and SFTP transfers checkbox, and then choose an action.

claims.claim: The FTP and SFTP activity supports Audit only, Block, Block with override and Allow.
claims.quote: Supported actions are Audit only, Block, Block with override, and Allow.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Once enabled, transfers are evaluated against the configured policy conditions, scope and enforcement actions.
claims.quote: Once enabled, FTP and SFTP transfer activities are evaluated using the conditions, scope, and enforcement actions configured in Endpoint DLP policies.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Full file evidence collection supports FTP and SFTP transfers.
claims.quote: FTP and SFTP transfers support full file evidence (FFE) collection.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Evidence collection can save a complete copy of a matched file when a transfer is attempted.
claims.quote: Enable evidence collection in Endpoint DLP settings and configure it in your DLP policy. When a user attempts to transfer a matched file, a complete copy can be saved.

claims.where: summary; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Block and Block with override are enforcement actions on FTP and SFTP transfer activities.
claims.quote: Admins can apply DLP actions such as audit, block, and block with override to FTP and SFTP transfer activities after enabling the capability in policy settings

claims.claim: Learn shows an end-user notification for a blocked FTP transfer.
claims.quote: Example of an end-user notification for a blocked FTP transfer:

claims.claim: Activity explorer is not a real-time view.
claims.quote: Activity explorer isn't a real-time view. Because its data comes from the Microsoft 365 unified audit log, activities appear on the same schedule as audit records — not the moment they occur.

claims.claim: Activity explorer reports up to 30 days of data.
claims.quote: Activity explorer reports on up to 30 days worth of data.

claims.claim: Devices report endpoint activities only while online.
claims.quote: Devices report endpoint activities only while they're online. An offline device backfills its activities after it reconnects.

claims.claim: A device that has not received a new or updated policy is not covered by that policy version.
claims.quote: Policies that are updated while a device is offline won't be pushed to that device. Similarly, such policies won't be enforced on that device, until the device is back online. However, the outdated policy that exists on the offline device will still be enforced.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/endpoint-dlp-learn-about#endpoint-dlp-and-offline-devices to sources for the statement about policy coverage before devices receive updates.

claims.claim: Devices must be online to receive policy updates.
claims.quote: Devices must be online for the policy update to happen.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not document automation or a PowerShell setting name for the FTP and SFTP action as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Endpoint DLP FTP SFTP EndpointDlpRestrictions PowerShell Set-DlpComplianceRule. Opened endpoint-dlp-ftp-sftp-short, New-DlpComplianceRule, Set-DlpComplianceRule and Set-PolicyConfig; searched the references for FTP/SFTP and EndpointDlpRestrictions; no FTP/SFTP setting documented.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Purview portal path to review activity is Data loss prevention > Activity explorer.

claims.where: controls[1].api; controls[1].note; Governance controls: second row
claims.claim: Export-ActivityExplorerData -StartTime <DateTime> -EndTime <DateTime> -OutputFormat Json exports Activity explorer events in Security & Compliance PowerShell without changing policy.
claims.quote:
This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
Export-ActivityExplorerData -StartTime "07/08/2022 07:15 AM" -EndTime "07/08/2022 11:08 AM" -OutputFormat Json
This example exports up to 100 records for the specified date range in Json format.

claims.claim: Evidence collection settings are in Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Data Loss Prevention > Endpoint DLP settings > Setup evidence collection for file activities on devices.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal and choose the Settings gear in the menu bar.
2. Choose Data Loss Prevention.
3. Select Endpoint DLP settings.
4. Expand Setup evidence collection for file activities on devices.

claims.claim: No automation is documented for configuring Endpoint DLP evidence collection and its storage selection.
claims.quote: Searched: Endpoint DLP evidence collection Set-PolicyConfig PowerShell storage CollectOriginalFile. Opened evidence setup, endpoint settings, Set-PolicyConfig, New-DlpComplianceRule and Set-DlpComplianceRule; no documented parameter for evidence collection or its storage selection.

claims.claim: Evidence collection also requires selecting Collect original file as evidence for all selected file activities on Endpoint and selecting FTP and SFTP transfers in the DLP rule.
claims.quote:
In Incident reports, select Collect original file as evidence for all selected file activities on Endpoint.
Select the activities for which you want to copy matched items to Azure storage, such as:
FTP and SFTP transfers

claims.claim: Per-device configuration and policy sync status are reviewed at Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Device onboarding > Devices.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Settings (gear icon in the upper right corner) > Device onboarding > Devices.

Navigate to Investigation & response > Hunting > Advanced hunting
Query the DeviceInfo table
Expand the DlpInfo column to view Endpoint DLP device details
DeviceInfo

| project DlpInfo
